earned_statement: The root stabilizers and ordered-duad stabilizers have the same abstract S3 element-order profile but are nonconjugate embeddings in the canonical five-point S5 action. Ordered-duad stabilizers are mixed-parity S3 subgroups with orbit profile 1+1+3, whereas root stabilizers are all-even S3 subgroups with orbit profile 2+3. Under the unique unordered-duad to inverse-root-pair bridge, every root stabilizer image is exactly the even setwise stabilizer of its assigned unordered duad. Thus the failure of ordered orientation propagation is an embedding obstruction, not a difference of abstract stabilizer type.
